blocks.content:
Article 6 deals with persons who migrated from Pakistan to India.
A person became a citizen if:
• He migrated before 19 July 1948 and was ordinarily resident in India, or
• He migrated after 19 July 1948 and was registered as a citizen.

This article is based on historical context of Partition.
Article 6 deals with persons who migrated from Pakistan to India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 6 provides citizenship rights to persons who migrated from Pakistan to India.
Persons migrating from Pakistan before 19 July 1948 needed to be ordinarily resident in India to gain citizenship.
Persons migrating from Pakistan after 19 July 1948 were required to be registered as citizens.
Article 7 applies to individuals who migrated from India to Pakistan after 1 March 1947.
Migrants to Pakistan generally lost Indian citizenship unless they returned under a permit for resettlement.
19 July 1948 is the pivotal cut-off date for Article 6 governing migrants from Pakistan.
1 March 1947 is the reference date for Article 7 regarding loss of citizenship upon migrating to Pakistan.
Resettlement permit exception: Migrants to Pakistan could regain Indian citizenship if they returned under a valid permit for resettlement.

blocks.content:
Article 7 applies to persons who migrated to Pakistan after 1 March 1947.

Such persons were generally not considered citizens of India, unless they later returned under a permit for resettlement.
